narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Well-Kept Messenger"**

ChatApp is the category-standard messenger played straight: a deep slate room rail on the left, a pale conversation pane on the right, the composer docked at the bottom. The bar is the finish of Telegram Web, WhatsApp Web and Discord. Nothing about the layout is novel on purpose. The craft is in the details a reviewer notices without being told: bubbles whose corners tighten where a run of messages joins, a stable colour per person, a send that settles from pending to delivered, a green presence dot on whoever is online, "is typing" in the header, a connection state that tells the truth, and people who are recognisable at a glance by photo or tone, with a profile one click from wherever their name appears.

The system is calm and dense in the way messengers are dense. One sans family (Figtree, self-hosted) carries every role. Colour does work: indigo marks what is yours or what you can act on, and the eight member tones tell people apart. Everything else is slate neutrals and 1px hairlines. Depth is close to flat, with soft ambient shadows only on things that float over the stream.

The build rejects the stock admin-template look: Material cards, centred forms floating on grey, and "Name: x Id: y" rows. Light and dark schemes are both first-class and follow the OS unless the user picks one.
keyCharacteristics: Three-pane messenger grammar: 300px slate rail, conversation pane, docked composer; phone collapses to list and room as separate screens.
Indigo is the single accent, reserved for own bubbles, primary actions and selection.
Eight stable hashed member tones for avatars and sender names.
Grouped bubble corners (18px outer, 6px joint, 4px tail).
One Figtree stack, 1px hairlines, inline 2px-stroke SVG icons on a 24px grid.
Live state is visible: optimistic pending, delivered check, arrival motion, presence dots, typing, unread counts, connection state.
Direct chats read as the other person (their name, photo or tone, presence); groups keep a room name and initials.
Names show as display name first, @username second; every person in the conversation pane opens a profile drawer.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Indigo means "yours" or "act here": own bubbles, primary actions, selection, focus, unread counts, links. It is never used for decoration, headings or incoming message text; a link inside an incoming bubble is an action and is the one indigo mark there.

rules.name: The Stable Tone Rule
rules.body: A person or room keeps one tone everywhere, derived from its numeric id (id mod 8) or an FNV-1a hash of the name. Never pick a tone by hand or by position in a list.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Slate is for the rail and things that float above the app (toasts, the auth showcase). The conversation and its controls sit on light surfaces. Do not put conversation content on slate.

rules.name: The Weight Not Family Rule
rules.body: Build hierarchy with Figtree's 400 / 600 / 700 weights and the sizes above. No second typeface, no uppercase labels, no tracked-out small caps.

rules.name: The Name Then Handle Rule
rules.body: A person is shown by display name, falling back to their username, everywhere a name appears: rail rows, headers, sender names, chips, search results, typing lines. The username appears only as a secondary "@username" line in muted ink. Initials come from the display name when one is set.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every `time` element and every count (unread badges, the composer counter, pager, section count) uses tabular numerals so numbers do not jitter. Times are 24-hour (HH:mm) in bubbles and in room rows alike; earlier days read "Yesterday" or a short date in the rail, and a bubble time carries the full date ("Tuesday 20 October 2026, 14:05") as its title.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: Only things that sit above the stream or the page get the Float shadow. Panes, bars, cards and forms stay flat and are separated by hairlines.

rules.name: The Ring Matches Ground Rule
rules.body: The presence dot's ring is the colour of whatever the avatar sits on, set through `--ring` by the host: slate rail, raised slate on hover, indigo on the active row, the darker footer, the white header. Any new surface that shows presence sets its ring, including its hover and active states.

dos: **Do** keep the three-pane messenger grammar: 300px slate rail, conversation pane with 64px header, composer docked at the bottom.
**Do** reserve indigo for own bubbles, primary actions, selection and focus.
**Do** colour every person through the tone pipe so their avatar and sender name match everywhere.
**Do** use the grouped bubble corners (18px, 6px joint, 4px tail) for any message-like element, including previews.
**Do** use inline SVG icons on the 24px grid with a 2px round stroke, sized 14-20px.
**Do** show live state truthfully: pending clock, delivered check, presence dots, typing line, unread badges, connection status, offline banner.
**Do** design every screen at phone width first-class, with safe-area insets on docked bars.
**Do** set `--ring` on any surface that hosts an avatar with presence, for every state of that surface.
**Do** keep times 24-hour (HH:mm) and tabular wherever they appear.
**Do** show people through the display-name pipe, with "@username" as the secondary line.
**Do** make another person's avatar or name in the conversation pane open their profile drawer.
**Do** honour prefers-reduced-motion by collapsing animation and transition to instant.
donts: **Don't** use Material cards, centred forms floating on grey, or "Name: x Id: y" label rows. Profile facts stack a small muted label over the value, divided by hairlines.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or a second accent colour.
**Don't** put a shadow on panes, bars or forms; only floating elements get the Float shadow.
**Don't** hand-pick member colours or reuse indigo as a member tone.
**Don't** use emoji or text glyphs as icons.
